programme.name: Universal Architectural Intelligence Engine — Faculty Binding and Register-Plane Reasoning Register
programme.mission: Reason continuously over Repository Truth. This programme does not replace Repository Truth and does not become a second authority over it. Every architectural faculty it names is already realised by a canonical owner and is bound to that owner by pointer; the binding is then measured, so a rename, a move or a deletion closes the gate instead of quietly invalidating the claim that the repository can reason about itself. The one thing this programme contributes that no located owner held is reasoning ACROSS the register plane: every existing analysis reasons within one substrate, and none reads the registers against each other. That cross-register measurement is declared, registered in the located analysis registry, and is the only capability this programme adds.
programme.disclosure: AUTHORITY = NONE. Nothing in this programme confers constitutional force, ratifies a determination, freezes anything, or supersedes a canonical owner. Every faculty binding is a pointer to an artifact that exists independently of this programme and remains owned by its own authority. The only facts asserted are measured from Repository Truth at render time and are re-measurable by re-running the engine. Standing is CERTIFIED-PROVISIONAL: tier T1 is vacant in the meta-constitutional registry, so no determination in this repository can reach RATIFIED.

admission_determination.basis: 00-CMG/CMG-000001 Article LXXVI.2(b) requires a candidate concept to be classified meta-constitutional or substantive and states that a substantive concept SHALL NOT be admitted into CMG. Architectural reasoning over repository artifacts governs no constitution and amends no constitutional process: it is substantive. Article LXXVII.2 therefore routes it to (a) REUSE where a located owner already holds the concern and (b) EXTEND where the concern lies inside a located owner's declared scope and is unaddressed there. Every faculty below takes one of those two outcomes or COMPOSE over several located owners. CREATE was rejected for all ten faculties: each is already realised, which is recorded per faculty in its reuse rationale. Consistent with this determination and with the observed content of the meta-constitutional registry — which recognizes only meta and family constitutional instruments and no substantive programme — this programme is deliberately absent from that registry, and the engine measures that absence rather than asserting it.
admission_determination.namespace_basis: No namespace token is claimed in the meta-constitutional registry. Article XLI.5 forbids an EXTEND from introducing a new authority, registry, lifecycle or namespace, and Article LXXVI reserves namespace admission to the meta layer for meta-constitutional constructs only. This programme's identifier is a programme home under 00-MASTER/, which is the convention every other substantive programme in this repository already follows.
rejected_alternatives: CREATE a new architectural reasoning engine in engine/ or platform/ — rejected: the eleven located owners bound below already realise all ten faculties, and a new engine would be a parallel authority over architectural reasoning, which 00-CMG/CMG-000001 CMG-INV-02 forbids.

CREATE a new analysis registry for architectural intelligence — rejected: 00-MASTER/UCOS-UAR-001 is the located owner of 'which analyses exist and who owns them' and is open by registration, so the contributed analyses below are entries in it rather than a second registry.
ADMIT this programme into the meta-constitutional registry — rejected under Article LXXVI.2(b): the concept is substantive.

REDESIGN the architectural layering of engine/graph, platform/repository_intelligence or engine/knowledge/integration — rejected: 00-MASTER/UCEF-000001 records that architectural redesign is not a stage of the constitutional evolution lifecycle, and a traversal requiring it has failed at reuse analysis and must return there.

ontology_anchors.basis: The capability universe already admits Reason as a first-class capability alongside Observe, Learn, Predict and Evolve, and is declared unlimited and extensible. Architectural reasoning is an instance of an ontology element that already exists, so this programme binds to it and introduces no new ontology element and no change to any declared cardinality (00-CMG/CMG-000001 Article XIV.7).

The ontology already places Intelligence as the layer that applies organised knowledge. This programme is an Intelligence-layer construct over the Knowledge layer held by the registers; it does not occupy or redefine the Wisdom layer, which governs intelligence and remains with the constitutional instruments.

Every node of the semantic graph this programme reasons over is already expressible in the universal ten-tuple — Identity, Relationship, Capability, Resource, State, Event, Policy, Authority, Constraint, Intent — so the graph needs no new meta-model.

faculties.name: Repository Semantic Graph
faculties.objective: One semantic graph over the entire repository, with every projection derived from it rather than stored beside it.
faculties.reuse: Already realised twice at two distinct scopes, and both are bound rather than merged. The certified knowledge graph is built over the canonical registers and is the corpus-scope graph; the repository graph is built over the real import surface and is the code-scope graph. The governing knowledge-graph architecture is explicit that there are several roots but one graph, so a third graph store is exactly what must not be created. This programme adds no node kind, no edge kind and no store.
faculties.gap: No single module bears the name used here. The capability is held by two owners at two scopes and is bound to both; the absence of one merged graph module is recorded rather than closed by building a third.

faculties.name: Architectural Reasoning Engine
faculties.objective: Reason across repository artifacts: stratification, layering inversions, blast radius, critical path, impact prediction and reachability.
faculties.reuse: Already realised as the architecture intelligence engine, which exposes layering, dependency intelligence, blast radius, critical path, impact prediction and semantic reachability over the one corpus graph, and carries pure strongly-connected-component, condensation and topological-order algorithms beside it. Those algorithms are reused, never rewritten: a second implementation of reachability would be a second answer to the same question.

faculties.name: Dependency Intelligence
faculties.objective: Detect dependency inconsistencies: cycles, unresolvable edges, inverted layers and the closure of what depends on what.
faculties.reuse: Already realised. Dependency intelligence derives transitive dependencies, fan-in, fan-out, hubs and circular-dependency reports over the corpus graph, and the repository dependency dimension derives the same closure over the real import graph. The constitutional dependency plane is separately validated by the meta-constitutional validator's acyclicity invariant, which is bound as evidence rather than reimplemented.

faculties.name: Ownership Intelligence
faculties.objective: Detect ownership conflicts: a concept with two owners, an owner with no concept, and a contested claim.
faculties.reuse: Already realised twice and both are bound. The ownership protocol is the fail-closed constitutional path: it requires exactly one owner and finds overlaps, refusing rather than defaulting. The repository ownership dimension derives declared owners from the code surface and marks a contested record. The meta-constitutional validator independently enforces injectivity of the concern-to-owner mapping and that every concern has exactly one located owner; that is bound as evidence, not restated.

faculties.name: Duplication Intelligence
faculties.objective: Detect duplicate concepts before a second home for one concept is created.
faculties.reuse: Already realised three times at three scopes, all bound. The duplicate-prevention engine screens a proposed artifact against the knowledge base and refuses on similarity. The repository duplicate dimension detects surface overlap and duplication across modules. The closure engine detects duplicate concepts, duplicate canonical homes and content-hash duplicates across the corpus, and the repository integration blueprint holds the duplicate register. Nothing here is a fourth detector.

faculties.name: Gap Intelligence
faculties.objective: Detect missing abstractions: structural gaps, completeness gaps, convention gaps and orphan units.
faculties.reuse: Already realised three times, all bound. The gap engine detects structural and completeness gaps over the truth snapshot and fingerprints the report so a gap set is comparable across runs. The repository gap dimension detects convention gaps over the code surface. The repository integration blueprint holds the gap register and classifies dead engines and unreachable entry points. This programme detects no new gap class of its own.

faculties.name: Evolution Intelligence
faculties.objective: Recommend constitutional evolution: what should change next, and under which located owner.
faculties.reuse: Already realised and registered as its own programme. Universal evolution intelligence binds the evolution capabilities to their homes; the autonomous evolution engine closes the observe-recommend loop over located owners; the constitutional evolution framework measures the fifteen-stage lifecycle any new construct must traverse; and the evolution governance model holds the normative process. A recommendation engine here would be a second voice on the same question.

faculties.name: Reuse Intelligence
faculties.objective: Recommend reuse before creation, and refuse creation where a located owner already holds the concern.
faculties.reuse: Already realised three times, all bound. The reuse engine assesses a proposed artifact and returns reuse, extend, compose or create; the constitutional pipeline runs that assessment as a mandatory fail-closed stage so creation cannot bypass it; the repository recommendation engine answers the same question over the code surface and returns reuse candidates; and the repository integration blueprint holds the reuse analysis. This programme's own admission determination was produced by applying this faculty, not by inventing another.

faculties.name: Constitutional Intelligence
faculties.objective: Verify constitutional consistency: that the constitutional plane holds together and that no artifact claims authority it does not have.
faculties.reuse: Already realised at three scopes, all bound. The integration constitution holds the laws that bind each stage of the constitutional path and refuses an ungrounded artifact. The meta-constitutional validator enforces twelve invariants over the constitutional registry with zero hardcoded enumeration members. The constitutional authority framework resolves authority and audits authority conflicts, and is the register to consult before any programme claims authority — including this one, which claims none. Adding a fourth constitutional checker would be the parallel machinery the meta layer forbids.

faculties.name: Completion Intelligence
faculties.objective: Determine repository completeness, and determine it as a computed verdict rather than a claim.
faculties.reuse: Already realised across four owners and bound to all of them, because completeness is answered at four different scopes and no single one of them is the whole answer. The completeness analyzer answers it as a validation dimension over the intelligence target; the reuse, duplication, conflict, gap and completeness verdicts of the reconciliation programme answer it over located owners; traceability closure answers whether every artifact traces with zero orphans; and freeze eligibility answers whether the repository has reached constitutional completion. A fifth completeness verdict would contradict one of the four.
faculties.gap: No single owner answers completeness for the whole repository. Four located owners answer it at four scopes and all four are bound; the absence of one merged verdict is recorded rather than closed by asserting a fifth.

contributed_analyses.name: register-plane-consistency
contributed_analyses.objective: Measure every path referenced by every declared register of the register plane and report the ones that no longer resolve.
contributed_analyses.why_not_already_owned: Each located analysis reasons within one substrate: the artifact registry validator checks the artifact registry, the meta-constitutional validator checks the constitutional registry, the platform binding engine checks its own bindings, and the analysis registry engine checks its own homes. None reads the registers against each other, so a register that drifts while its own owner stays green is invisible. This analysis is that cross-register reading and nothing more; it re-derives no substrate and duplicates no owner's verdict.

contributed_analyses.name: faculty-binding-resolution
contributed_analyses.objective: Measure whether every named architectural faculty still resolves to a home and a symbol that exist, and to at least one analysis registered in the located analysis registry.
contributed_analyses.why_not_already_owned: The capability catalogue records that a capability exists and where it lives; the analysis registry records that an analysis exists and who owns it. Neither answers whether a named architectural faculty is realised by a registered analysis at a resolving home, which is the join across the two. The platform binding engine performs the analogous join for platform capabilities but is scoped to that agreement and must not be widened to cover a different faculty set.

contributed_analyses.name: architectural-faculty-closure
contributed_analyses.objective: Measure whether the faculty dependency relation is closed and acyclic and whether every declared register of the plane is claimed by at least one faculty.
contributed_analyses.why_not_already_owned: Dependency closure is owned at the artifact, program and constitutional planes by three located owners. None of them holds a faculty plane, because none of them names faculties. This analysis measures closure over the faculty relation this programme declares, and asserts nothing about the planes those owners already own.

baseline.basis: the contract binds every change from this baseline forward; the baseline record is immutable and is not edited by this change (Rule R-1)

change_classification.label: New capability
change_classification.basis: Exactly one class from the located closed register. The three analyses this programme contributes — reading the declared registers against each other, resolving each named faculty to a registered analysis, and closure over the faculty relation — had no prior existence anywhere in the corpus, which is the definition of this class. It is NOT an extension: an extension expands an existing capability's scope, and no existing capability read across registers to be expanded. It is NOT documentation: the discharge is executable and gate-bound, not a consolidation of existing knowledge. Note the distinction the record must preserve: the CHANGE CLASS is new capability, while the DISPOSITION of each of the ten named architectural faculties is REUSE or COMPOSE over owners that already exist, and CREATE was rejected for all ten. A new change class is not a new authority.
